findings.severity: textual inconsistency / potential fixture accounting ambiguity
findings.claim: FR-INT-063 AC-INT-063-02 says CASE-INT-063-02a–02g are independently evaluated, while its own description and FV define CASE-INT-063-02g as a composite legacy index whose out-of-order and duplicate predicates are independently tested by CASE-INT-063-04g/04h. NFR-063-02/NFRV-063-02 count 04a–04h, not 02g.
findings.practical_impact: A reader using the AC summary literally may require/count an extra composite fixture or double-count two predicates, while L10/NFR treat it as a non-independent index. Detailed oracle and owner behavior in 04g/04h is present, so this is a trace/fixture-accounting ambiguity rather than evidence of a false positive acceptance path.
findings.fixed_parent_check: L2-063 / L11-063 require historical outcomes to stay attached to their original episode and not overwrite current judgment; they do not require an extra composite test.
findings.recommendation: At the next authorized text revision, clarify that 02g is an index and that its two predicates are independently covered by 04g/04h; do not add a fixture or change parent meaning. No immediate blocker assertion.
